meta.scope: Indonesia Batch 9 — Deeper health-system detail, fiscal/tax structure, specific commodity trade-partner patterns, and further Java municipal densification.

candidates.title: Health Statistics Profile
candidates.description: Annual BPS publication presenting population health, child health, reproductive-age women’s health and household health expenditures, drawn primarily from Susenas. Disaggregated by province, urban/rural, age, education and economic status.

candidates.title: Health facilities statistics (hospitals, puskesmas by province)
candidates.description: Official counts of general hospitals, specialised hospitals, and community health centres (puskesmas) with and without inpatient care, by province. Reveals strong concentration of higher-level facilities on Java.
candidates.notes: Supply-side health-system node with clear spatial gradient.

candidates.title: Tax revenue structure and actual government revenues
candidates.description: Detailed composition of actual government revenues: income tax (oil/gas and non-oil/gas), VAT, excises, international trade taxes, natural-resource non-tax revenues, etc. Primary statistical view of the tax and non-tax revenue base.
candidates.notes: Structural fiscal node. Indonesia’s tax-to-GDP ratio remains relatively low by regional standards; commodity-linked revenues remain visible.

candidates.title: Tax-to-GDP ratio and fiscal capacity indicators
candidates.publisher: Ministry of Finance / international compilations citing official data
candidates.description: Official and widely cited tax-to-GDP ratio and related fiscal-capacity measures. Continuously referenced in domestic fiscal debates and international comparisons.
referenced_by: Tax revenue structure and APBN statistics

candidates.title: Export statistics by country of destination (major partners)
candidates.description: Merchandise export values and volumes broken down by destination country. China, United States, Japan, India, ASEAN partners and others appear as recurring major markets; the composition interacts with commodity mix (palm oil, coal, nickel products, manufactures).
candidates.notes: Partner-side densification of the external-trade cluster.

candidates.title: Commodity × destination trade patterns (palm oil, coal, nickel, manufactures)
candidates.publisher: Derived from BPS Foreign Trade Statistics
candidates.description: Statistical patterns linking major export commodities to their principal destination markets. Forms the empirical backbone of discussions about China demand for nickel and coal, Indian and other markets for palm oil, and diversified manufactured-goods destinations.
referenced_by: Palm-oil, coal, nickel and manufacturing export nodes
candidates.notes: Relational trade node that tightens edges between commodity and partner clusters.

candidates.title: West Java (Jawa Barat) provincial and major municipal statistical profile
candidates.publisher: BPS Jawa Barat / local BPS offices
candidates.description: Provincial and selected municipal statistics for West Java — the most populous province, major manufacturing and peri-urban extension of the Jakarta metropolitan system.
candidates.notes: Densification of the western Java industrial-population belt.

candidates.title: Central Java (Jawa Tengah) provincial and Magelang-context profile
candidates.publisher: BPS Jawa Tengah / local BPS offices
candidates.description: Provincial statistics for Central Java and the surrounding highland corridor that includes Magelang. Important agricultural, manufacturing and cultural region.
candidates.notes: Central Java densification; direct spatial parent of the Magelang local node.

candidates.title: East Java (Jawa Timur) provincial and Malang-context profile
candidates.publisher: BPS Jawa Timur / local BPS offices
candidates.description: Provincial statistics for East Java — second-most populous province, major industrial and agricultural region that includes Malang as an important secondary urban and educational centre.
candidates.notes: East Java densification; direct spatial parent of the Malang local node.

candidates.title: Indonesia health–fiscal–trade-partner–Java densification meta-node
candidates.publisher: Derived from BPS, Ministry of Health, Ministry of Finance and trade statistics
candidates.description: Meta-node binding the Health Statistics Profile, health-facilities counts, tax-revenue structure, tax-to-GDP indicators, export-by-destination and commodity–partner patterns, and further Java provincial densification (West, Central, East Java) into a coherent health–fiscal–trade–spatial layer.
referenced_by: All detailed nodes in this batch
Earlier BPJS, APBN, trade, Magelang/Malang and Java-core nodes
